reference-only: checkpoint atomicity/dedup is useful evidence, but generic scraping/MCP and automatic work replay broaden authority and can replay non-idempotent jobs.
rejected-with-reason: scraped public configuration datasets are untrusted remote inputs, license provenance is unclear, and they cannot become authoritative profile state.
reference-only: rich desktop process/connection UI is useful product evidence, but target lacks a canonical cross-runtime flow registry and desktop per-app authority remains unsupported.
reference-only: external sing-box validation/probing is a useful oracle, but AGPL code and a second subscription/runtime owner are not adopted.
superseded: LumiNet already owns WARP/MASQUE scanning/runtime with bounded real-handshake qualification; donor staging does not justify another WARP authority.
adapted: repeated quality samples exposed temporal jitter as a stable ranking discriminator; unsafe worker counts and arbitrary aggregate weights are not adopted.
reference-only: connection-table UX is valuable, but its backend assumes a canonical connections API LumiNet does not yet have across all runtimes.
rejected-with-reason: GTK binding generation targets the wrong product stack and adds build/runtime complexity without LumiNet semantic value.
superseded: feeder/fetcher/cancellation patterns overlap LumiNet scanner scheduling and diagnostics; no second scanner framework is adopted.
hardened: strict IP declared-length checks and bounded conflict-aware defragmentation semantics harden existing LumiNet packet owners; generic live packet crafting is not added.
adapted: real TTL-scoped traceroute semantics replace LumiNet fake repeated-connect tracing; donor CLI/runtime packaging is not imported.
rejected-with-reason: legacy SSH obfuscation uses deliberately weak anti-scanning crypto and would fork obsolete SSH protocol/runtime authority.
adapted: finite follow-up and bounded Retry-After semantics harden LumiNet subscription HTTP resilience without importing the HTTP stack.
